body.statement: Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), \(L=|\mathrm{LIT}|\), and \(n=|V|\). If the oracle-instance \(\mathsf X_{\mathrm{phys}}\) is feasible, then it has a lexicographically canonical accepting uniform certificate with at most \(k\) nonempty records, one owned transcript schema for each factor, no empty-ownership record, and no larger cost than any accepting acquired collection. Every transcript has at most \(n\) strict restrictions and at most \(8(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\) bits. Consequently \(N_E\le B_{\mathrm{cert}}=k(m+L+k+n(1+L))+8k(n+1)^2\lceil\log_2(n+L+k+2)\rceil\le8k(N_{\mathrm{in}}+1)^4\). Thus the lexicographically first optimum \(E^{\star}\) exists and its certificate length is polynomial in the structural input and \(k\); oracle replies are separately charged by \(N_{\mathcal O}\).
body.justification: The bound separates compact existential certificate data from potentially large, explicitly charged oracle support replies.
body.gap: Fixed-source completeness provides no canonical polynomial bound on an endogenous physical acquisition certificate or its transcript schema.
body.consumer: The exact optimizer can bound certificate enumeration while reporting source-interface cost separately.
